candidates.rationale: Frequency of days per month where price direction and volume change agree proxies genuine participation behind a move rather than its mere existence; crossing with leverage tests whether this order-flow confirmation matters more for financially riskier firms.

A rising or falling trailing-volume percentile signals attention migrating into or out of a name; taking its own time-derivative isolates a genuine shift in relative liquidity standing from the stock's static liquidity tier.

Short-window dispersion of volume around its own longer baseline flags episodic, information-driven liquidity events distinct from steady-state turnover; crossing with ROE tests whether such spikes are more informative for more profitable firms.

Counting recent days of unusually heavy dollar volume detects bursts of trading attention; for asset-rich, thinly-followed firms (high book-per-share) such bursts more plausibly reflect fresh information than routine turnover.

How much a stock's cross-sectional liquidity ranking bounces around over a month proxies transient, uninformed order flow versus a structurally stable liquidity tier, a distinct signal from the liquidity level itself.

True volume-weighting of the daily high-low range lets well-participated, high-volume days dominate the volatility estimate over noisy thin-volume gaps, giving a liquidity-conditioned measure of range rather than a simple average.

A recency-weighted dollar-volume trend running ahead of its own medium-term average signals freshly building attention; for high-operating-margin firms that attention should convert into more efficient price discovery.

Multiplying a stock's liquidity level by its own recent liquidity acceleration isolates a crowding effect, where names that are already liquid and seeing activity build further reflect converging institutional order flow.

Ranking overnight gap magnitude jointly with liquidity level tests whether gaps get absorbed efficiently into price in deep, high-volume names versus persisting or reverting in thin ones with fragile order books.

The swing between a stock's calmest and busiest trading day, scaled by its typical volume, flags episodic event-driven liquidity; pairing with ROA tests whether such spikes are absorbed more efficiently into price for fundamentally productive firms.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.

Direction for this island

Archive coverage so far. Each niche is (IC half-life bucket / data family /
turnover bucket). Aim at the emptiest ones: a factor that fills an empty niche
is worth more to this search than a slightly better version of a full one.

Sub-expressions already heavily used by the published Alpha101 set. Reusing one
of these wholesale will be rejected as a paraphrase; they are listed so you can
avoid them, not so you can vary them cosmetically.
  (($high + $low) / 2)   (in 5 published alphas)
  ($high + $low)   (in 5 published alphas)
  DELAY($close, 1)   (in 5 published alphas)
  TS_DELTA($close, 1)   (in 5 published alphas)
  TS_MEAN($volume, 20)   (in 5 published alphas)

  (1e-08 + TS_MEAN($volume, 20))   (in 4 published alphas)
  ($close - DELAY($close, 1))   (in 4 published alphas)
  TS_DELTA($close, 7)   (in 4 published alphas)
  (((DELAY($close, 20) - DELAY($close, 10)) / 10) - ((DELAY($close, 10) - $close) / 10))   (in 3 published alphas)
  ((DELAY($close, 20) - DELAY($close, 10)) / 10)   (in 3 published alphas)
  (($close - DELAY($close, 1)) * -(1))   (in 3 published alphas)

Working memory: rules written after earlier rounds on this island, oldest first. Apply them.
  1. ($close - TS_MIN($low,w)) / (TS_MAX($high,w) - TS_MIN($low,w)) is window-stable: the 21-day and 42-day versions correlated at rho 0.950. A window change alone will not clear correlation on this formula; change which price field anchors the numerator/denominator instead.
  2. Ratios normalized by TS_STD($high-$low,10) collide on the denominator alone: (close-low) and (high-close) numerators over that same denominator shared 7 nodes and were rejected together. Changing only the numerator on a reused volatility-normalizer subtree is not enough; also change the window or the volatility measure.
  3. CS_ZSCORE($operating_margin) - CS_ZSCORE(TS_RANK($dollar_volume,252)) failed coverage (0.825) even though the price side has full history; the fundamental's own sparsity is the binding constraint. When pairing any fundamental with a price/volume leg, keep that leg's window at 63 days or less.
  4. 3 of 20 proposals this round (15%) were exact duplicates of an earlier proposal in the same batch (a book_per_share/close x roe product, an eps/low-minus-return spread, a high-close-over-dollar_volume ratio). Check candidates against everything already proposed this run, not only the persistent archive.
  5. Pure price/volume products need no fundamental leg: CS_ZSCORE/CS_DEMEAN of a range-or-displacement leg ($high-$low, TS_DELTA($open,w), TS_STD($open,w)) times CS_ZSCORE/TS_RANK of a volume or $dollar_volume leg took 5 of 9 accepts and the round's top 3 fitnesses (4.592, 3.613, 3.338). Keep mining this pairing across windows and field pairs.
  6. 42% of rejects (8/19) were in-round duplicates, clustered on TS_MIN($low,21) range/position ratios and $asset_turnover/$earnings_per_share crossed with TS_MEAN or TS_STD($return). Dedupe every new proposal against everything already queued this round, not just the archive.
  7. A kernel that fails cheap_screen bare can pass once crossed with an unused fundamental rank: ($dollar_volume/$volume)/$open failed alone (|t| 0.54) but hit 0.947 once multiplied by CS_RANK($operating_margin). Retry marginal bare rejects with a fresh fundamental multiplier instead of discarding them.
  8. Swapping the price field in an accepted shape does not decorrelate: $adj_close vs $close in a book_per_share ratio hit rho 1.000, and $close vs $open inside a TS_DELTA(...,5) spread leg hit 0.839. Vary the operator or window, not which of open/high/low/close/adj_close fills a slot.
  9. Raw-$return kernels without a fundamental partner stayed weak: SIGN($return) x CS_RANK($volume) and COUNT($volume>DELAY($volume,1),10) x CS_RANK($return) both failed cheap_screen. COUNT-style and sign-style kernels need a fundamental rank on the other leg to clear screen, as already proven for $roa.
  10. CS_RANK(TS_STD($return,5)) and CS_ZSCORE(TS_MEAN($dollar_volume,21)) are now saturated as standalone fragments, each triggering an archive_subtree reject regardless of the paired leg. Don't reuse either verbatim even with a new partner.
  11. This round's accepts skewed heavily to price_volume niches (7 of 9); only one touched a fundamental (operating_margin, landing in slow/mixed/high). If broader fundamental/mixed niche coverage matters, prioritize fundamental-crossed proposals next round before price_volume slots fill further.
  12. MIN($return,0) (raw downside truncation, no fundamental) missed cheap_screen at |t| 0.99, right at the threshold. Unlike EPS downside truncation which is productive, truncating raw $return alone is unproven; pair with a fundamental rather than resubmitting bare.

For each proposal give a one-line economic rationale: what mechanism would make
this predict returns. "It is a momentum variant" is not a mechanism.
Leave `parent_ids` empty and `changed_node` empty for EXPLORE.
